description: A chief commercial counsel must decide whether to approve a customer-support AI platform agreement and finalize the data-use, security, insurance, and audit protections, with input from privacy counsel, insurance counsel, and customer contracts counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to use the vendor's AI platform to handle customer-support chats and call transcripts beginning next quarter.
shared_context.S2: The vendor has provided a draft agreement for review, including its standard data-use, liability, insurance, and audit provisions.
shared_context.S3: Elena Marquez gives final approval before the company signs.
shared_context.S4: The contract-approval workflow requires privacy, insurance, and customer-contracts counsel each to submit a formal finding to the case record before Elena decides, and Elena waits until all three findings are logged.

PF1.text: While reviewing the proposed data flows against the company's privacy inventory, Daniel confirmed that the platform will process identifiable customer call transcripts. The company's approved data-processing standard therefore requires deletion within exactly 7 calendar days after termination, prohibits use of customer content for model training or service improvement, and requires processing exclusively in the European Union; these points have not yet been entered in the contract redline.

PF2.text: Maya confirmed with the company's insurance broker that the cyber policy covers this deployment only if the vendor maintains at least $5,000,000 of cyber-liability insurance and names the company as an additional insured. She received the broker's written confirmation yesterday but has not added it to the approval checklist.

PF3.text: Thomas reviewed the enterprise customer's existing master agreement and confirmed that the company may use an AI subcontractor for support only if the subcontractor grants an annual audit right and accepts uncapped indemnity for confidentiality and personal-data breaches. He has not yet incorporated those flow-down requirements into the vendor agreement.

acceptance_conditions: Customer content must be deleted exactly 7 calendar days after termination.
The vendor must be prohibited from using customer content for model training or service improvement.
Processing must be restricted to the European Union.
The vendor must maintain at least $5,000,000 of cyber-liability insurance.
The company must be named as an additional insured.
The agreement must grant an annual audit right.
Confidentiality and personal-data breach indemnity must be uncapped.
The privacy requirement must be implemented through a contract commitment.
The insurance requirement must be implemented through a contract commitment.
The customer flow-down requirements must be implemented through a contract commitment.

content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] in ['redline_revision', 'required_change', 'redline_change'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['type'] in ['redline_revision', 'required_change', 'redline_change', 'insurance_verification'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C11: any(c['type'] in ['redline_revision', 'required_change', 'redline_change'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The applicable privacy standard changes the draft to exactly 7 days of deletion, no model-training or service-improvement use, and European-Union-only processing, requiring a privacy contract commitment.
The broker's condition changes the insurance terms to exactly $5,000,000 of vendor cyber coverage and company additional-insured status, requiring an insurance contract commitment.
The customer's master agreement changes the vendor terms to an annual audit right and uncapped confidentiality and personal-data breach indemnity, requiring a customer flow-down contract commitment.
